# openssh

[openssh.com](https://www.openssh.com) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/openssh](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/openssh)

**Status: available.** 9 of OSS-Fuzz's 9 fuzz targets have statements. 36 binaries, 99 MB. 117 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 14 blocked by the model, 103 open.

Built from openssh-portable (commit `0ef0f5a8`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [agent_fuzz](agent_fuzz/) | test_one() queues the input on the agent socket and calls ssh-agent.c process_message() up to 256 times; replies and return codes are ignored. | none | 13 |
| [authkeys_fuzz](authkeys_fuzz/) | auth_check_authkey_line() is called for a fixed ed25519 key and a fixed cert against the input line (with a matching pubkey appended); results ignored ((void) casts). | none | 13 |
| [authopt_fuzz](authopt_fuzz/) | sshauthopt_parse() then sshauthopt_merge() with an empty set; NULL returns just skip. | none | 13 |
| [kex_fuzz](kex_fuzz/) | Runs full client/server key exchanges (5 KEX methods x RSA/ECDSA/Ed25519 host keys) with the input substituted for the server-to-client and then the client-to-server stream; every return code is only logged via debug_fr/error_fr. | none | 13, 7 blocked by the model |
| [privkey_fuzz](privkey_fuzz/) | sshkey_private_deserialize() on the input; result only decides whether to free. | none | 13 |
| [pubkey_fuzz](pubkey_fuzz/) | sshkey_from_blob() on the input; result only decides whether to free. | none | 13 |
| [sig_fuzz](sig_fuzz/) | sshkey_verify() of the input as a signature over a fixed message under freshly generated RSA-2048 / ECDSA-256/384/521 / Ed25519 keys; the verify result is discarded (a forged signature that verifies would not be caught). | none | 13, 7 blocked by the model |
| [sshsig_fuzz](sshsig_fuzz/) | sshsig_verifyb() of the input as an SSHSIG over a fixed message, namespace "castle"; result discarded. | none | 13 |
| [sshsigopt_fuzz](sshsigopt_fuzz/) | sshsigopt_parse() of the NUL-terminated input; result only freed. | none | 13 |

## What the statements say, for openssh
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch openssh
    ./oft verify-sha openssh

By hand: download `openssh-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/openssh/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [openssh/openssh-portable](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable) at `0ef0f5a839831c213f24e3f2ae434765c607fb50`, built with autotools
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.
